relevance_note: Describes an adult Japanese man with HA20 carrying a germline TNFAIP3 variant: "The results revealed a heterozygous variant of the TNFAIP3 gene, specifically c.259C>T (R87X) (Table 1)."
method_note: Read only the paper, the schema and the rules; every quote was copied by hand and checked to occur verbatim in the paper (no script transcribed any table). Scope: the index case (II-3), his three relatives described in relation to him (II-2, III-1, III-3; symptoms suggestive of HA20, no genetic testing performed), and the 11 previously published patients of the literature table (Table 2 rows 2-12). Table 2 row 1 is the present case, i.e. II-3, so it gets no separate row; its variant and features are merged into II-3. Group-level mentions of other patients (the Zhou et al. cohort, 71 East Asian cases, 177 cases in a systematic review, and the two earlier families reported to carry the same variant) give no individual-level facts and got no rows. Contradictions and ambiguities: (1) Table 1 and the text give the TNFAIP3 variant as c.259C>T / p.Arg87Ter, but the Figure 2 legend prints 'R87X: TNFAIP3 gene c.159C>T variant (present case)'; the c.259C>T form was recorded. (2) For II-3 the text gives recurrent oral ulcers since 10 years of age and symptoms at 28 years of age, whereas Table 2 row 1 gives onset at 18 years; the table value was used for age at onset and the discrepancy is noted here. (3) The paper reports folliculitis in the patient's history while the admission examination found 'no new skin lesions, including erythema nodosum'; the history of folliculitis was recorded as observed, the absence of new lesions and of erythema nodosum as excluded, and the composite checklist item 'skin lesions (rash, folliculitis, erythema nodosum)' as observed. (4) The paper reports suspected atypical mycobacterial infection and imaging suggestive of nontuberculous mycobacterial infection, but cultures were negative, so no recurrent-infection feature was recorded. Stacked cells: in Table 2 the cells of the columns 'Age at onset/Current age' and 'Sex/Ethnicity' each hold two values separated by '/'; the two parts are labelled in the header row, so the first value was read as the onset/sex and the second as the current age/ethnicity. No other multi-patient stacked cell was read positionally. Table 1 is one patient's variant list; only its TNFAIP3 row is a TNFAIP3 variant, and the NLRP3 and PLCG2 rows were not extracted (other genes, assessed as of 'limited disease relevance'). The Table 2 note 'The genotype of all cases was heterozygous' is a statement about the named group of Table 2 cases and was used for zygosity of those patients. cites_prior_report_of_same_patients is false because the paper never states that its own patients were published before; a negative has no supporting quote, so its span is null. Normal or negative findings were recorded as the abnormality they rule out (D-27), e.g. 'liver dysfunction' excluded from 'no evidence of liver or kidney dysfunction', and 'positive autoantibodies other than anti-nuclear antibody' excluded from the negative antibody panel.
